# Clover IIIF

> Clover IIIF is a viewer as distinctive as your collections: design the user experience that you imagine for your IIIF resources, Manifests and Collections. A project of Northwestern University Libraries. These docs lead with Clover 4, `@nulib/clover`, which is in development and not yet on npm. Clover 3.x, `@samvera/clover-iiif`, is the earlier version: it is still the one on npm, and its docs are kept under /docs/3.x/ for reference only. Do not take 3.x's API or behavior as Clover 4's.

## Clover 4 (current docs)

- [Get Started](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs): what Clover is, installing it, what each import ships, the web component, and moving from 3.x
- [Viewer](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/viewer): the ready-made Viewer, its templates and what it handles
- [Templates](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/viewer#templates): Default, Document and Gallery
- [Composing Layouts](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/composing): a layout of your own from Clover's parts, hooks, renderers, languages and styles
- [Cookbook Recipes](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/cookbook): every IIIF Cookbook recipe, to open in the Viewer
- Components: [Content](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/content), [Canvas](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/canvas), [Items](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/items), [Panel](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/panel), [Map](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/map), and the [Primitives](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/primitives), one part per IIIF descriptive property
- [i18n](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/i18n): the languages Clover ships, how it chooses one, and adding a language
- Source: [nulib-ds/clover](https://github.com/nulib-ds/clover), the package in `packages/clover`

## Clover 3.x (earlier version, reference only)

- [Clover 3.x](https://nulib-ds.github.io/clover/docs/3.x): the docs of `@samvera/clover-iiif`, whose source is [samvera-labs/clover-iiif](https://github.com/samvera-labs/clover-iiif)
